facts.text: This sequel was shot as "Class of 2001: The Substitute" and kept that title in France. That's why a character says the Kennedy High incidents happened two years ago.
Director Spiro Razatos was a stuntman first. He later became a stunt coordinator on Fast & Furious, Captain America: Civil War and Venom.
Original Class of 1999 director Mark L. Lester reportedly just collected a paycheck on this sequel and didn't take part in making it.
Sasha Mitchell came in fresh from Kickboxer sequels. He started lifting weights right before making the kickboxing movies in the early 1990s.
Nick Cassavetes is nearly a foot taller than his dad, filmmaker John Cassavetes. He got the height from his mom, Gena Rowlands.
Budget cuts hit hard: the original Class of 1999 had three killer androids and flashy effects. This sequel has just one and cut the effects.
The film reuses flashback footage from Class of 1999 (1990) to tie itself to the earlier android-teacher story.
Screenwriter Mark Sevi also wrote Ghoulies IV, Scanner Cop II: Volkin's Revenge and Pterodactyl.
Rick Hill (G.D. Ash) was a Georgia Tech running back and played in the Canadian Football League before acting.
Sasha Mitchell played Patrick Duffy's nephew on both Dallas and Step by Step. He was fired from Step by Step for breaking probation.
Sasha Mitchell's real family name is Muchnik, and he loves building and collecting Harley-Davidsons.
In the principal's early scene he says "If President Clinton hadn't been indicted..." Clinton was impeached in 1999, years after this was shot.
Germany cut 92 seconds from this film, then indexed it from 1994 to 2019. An uncut version got a "not under 18" rating only in 2024.
The UK video release lost 9 seconds for an '18' rating. The later DVD was passed uncut with the same rating.
Vidmark Entertainment released this on VHS in March 1994. It never got a Region 1 DVD, though Region 2 did.
A trivia note: an early shot of John eating in his car was a subtle hint about what he really is. Real androids don't eat dinner.
Nick Cassavetes later directed The Notebook, which he reportedly considers his worst film, and John Q. He also acted in Face/Off.
The Class of... series began with Class of 1984 (1982). All three films are only loosely related.
